literal: Dou Tai; Wei Jing; Lou Zhao; nephew Rui; Kudie Gan; son Shiwen; Han Gui; Pan Le
idiomatic: Dou Tai; Wei Jing; Lou Zhao; nephew Rui; Kudie Gan; son Shiwen; Han Gui; Pan Le

literal: Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
idiomatic: Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.

literal: His family originally came from Guanjin in Qinghe; his great-grandfather Luo was general of the Wei garrison at Tongwan and settled on the northern frontier.
idiomatic: His family originally came from Guanjin in Qinghe; his great-grandfather Luo was general of the Wei garrison at Tongwan and settled on the northern frontier.

literal: His father Yue, when Poliuhan Baling rebelled at the end of Wei, held firm with the garrison general Yang Jun and was killed in action.
idiomatic: His father Yue, when Poliuhan Baling rebelled at the end of Wei, held firm with the garrison general Yang Jun and was killed in action.

literal: When Tai rose high, Yue was posthumously made minister of education.
idiomatic: When Dou Tai rose high, his father Yue was posthumously made minister of education.

literal: At first Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst up as though rain were coming; she went out to the courtyard to watch and saw lightning dazzle her eyes and driving rain spatter down; waking in a sweat of alarm, she conceived.
idiomatic: At first Dou Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst up as though rain were coming; she went out to the courtyard to watch and saw lightning dazzle her eyes and driving rain spatter down; waking in a sweat of alarm, she conceived.

literal: When her term passed without birth, she was greatly afraid.
idiomatic: When her term passed without birth, she was greatly afraid.

literal: A witch said, "Cross the river and wash your skirt, and the birth will surely come easily.
idiomatic: A witch said, "Cross the river and wash your skirt, and the birth will surely come easily.

literal: " She went at once toward the water.
idiomatic: " She went at once toward the water.

literal: Suddenly she saw a man who said, "You will bear a noble son; move south.
idiomatic: Suddenly she saw a man who said, "You will bear a noble son; move south.

literal: " Tai's mother obeyed.
idiomatic: " Dou Tai's mother obeyed.

literal: Soon afterward Tai was born.
idiomatic: Soon afterward Dou Tai was born.

literal: When he grew up, he was skilled at riding and archery and possessed courage and strategy.
idiomatic: When he grew up, he was skilled at riding and archery and possessed courage and strategy.

literal: Tai's father and elder brother died in battle at the garrison; Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: Dou Tai's father and elder brother died in battle at the garrison; Dou Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.

literal: For following the campaign against Xing Gao and meriting success, he was granted the title Viscount of Guanga.
idiomatic: For following the campaign against Xing Gao and meriting success, he was granted the title viscount of Guanga.

literal: When Shenwu became governor of Jin Province, he requested Tai as garrison-city commander and staff officer for military affairs.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan became governor of Jin Province, he requested Dou Tai as garrison-city commander and staff officer for military affairs.

literal: He rose in succession to palace attendant, grand commander of the capital region, and soon afterward also served as censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to palace attendant, grand commander of the capital region, and soon afterward also served as censor-in-chief.

literal: Tai, holding high office by merit and kinship, made few impeachments, yet the hundred officials feared him.
idiomatic: Dou Tai, holding high office by merit and kinship, made few impeachments, yet the hundred officials feared him.

literal: In the third year of Tianping, Shenwu campaigned west and ordered Tai to enter by Tong Pass.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping, Gao Huan campaigned west and ordered Dou Tai to enter by Tong Pass.

literal: In the fourth year Tai reached Little Pass, was ambushed by Emperor Wen of Zhou, and his whole force was destroyed; Tai killed himself.
idiomatic: In the fourth year Dou Tai reached Little Pass, was ambushed by Yuwen Tai, and his whole force was destroyed; Dou Tai killed himself.

literal: At first, when Tai was about to set out from Ye, a ballad of the nun Huihua in Ye said, "Commandery Chief Dou goes and does not return.
idiomatic: At first, when Dou Tai was about to set out from Ye, a ballad of the nun Huihua in Ye said, "Commandery Chief Dou goes and does not return.

literal: " Before he marched, at the third watch of the night, suddenly several thousand men in red robes and caps entered the censorate, saying they had come "to arrest Censor Dou"; the night guards and clerks were all alarmed; the figures entered several rooms and in a moment were gone.
idiomatic: " Before he marched, at the third watch of the night, suddenly several thousand men in red robes and caps entered the censorate, saying they had come "to arrest Censor Dou"; the night guards and clerks were all alarmed; the figures entered several rooms and in a moment were gone.

literal: At dawn they looked and the locks were unchanged; only then did they know these were not human beings.
idiomatic: At dawn they looked and the locks were unchanged; only then did they know these were not human beings.

literal: All knew he was doomed to defeat.
idiomatic: All knew he was doomed to defeat.

literal: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhen.

literal: Tai's wife was the younger sister of Empress Lou Wuming.
idiomatic: Dou Tai's wife was the younger sister of Empress Lou Wuming.

literal: Although Tai was treated as kin, his fame and achievement were his own.
idiomatic: Although Dou Tai was treated as kin, his fame and achievement were his own.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, sacrifice was announced at his tomb.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, sacrifice was announced at his tomb.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Shenwu's temple court.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.

literal: His son Xiaojing succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xiaojing succeeded.

literal: He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.
idiomatic: He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.

literal: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.
idiomatic: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.

literal: In Qin and Han the office of frontier scout was established; an ancestor who had held that post took it as the clan surname.
idiomatic: In Qin and Han the office of frontier scout was established; an ancestor who had held that post took it as the clan surname.

literal: Jing was warm by nature and possessed a chivalrous spirit.
idiomatic: Jing was warm by nature and possessed a chivalrous spirit.

literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing entered Du Luozhou's army together with Shenwu and then both returned to Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing entered Du Luozhou's army together with Gao Huan and then both returned to Erzhu Rong.

literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed baron of Boye County.
idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed baron of Boye County.

literal: Later he followed Shenwu in raising troops at Xindu.
idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising troops at Xindu.

literal: At the Battle of Hanling, only the force Jing commanded suffered defeat.
idiomatic: At the Battle of Hanling, only the force Jing commanded suffered defeat.

literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.

literal: Soon afterward his rank was advanced to duke.
idiomatic: Soon afterward his rank was advanced to duke.

literal: Jing's wife, Lady Changshan, was Shenwu's elder sister.
idiomatic: Jing's wife, Lady Changshan, was Gao Huan's elder sister.

literal: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudie Gan were often entrusted with weighty command, yet he could not put aside profit; Shenwu frequently reproved him for it.
idiomatic: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudie Gan were often entrusted with weighty command, yet he could not put aside profit; Gao Huan frequently reproved him for it.

literal: Transferred to governor of Ji Province, he again took large bribes and pressed laborers into a hunt in which three hundred men died.
idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Ji Province, he again took large bribes and pressed laborers into a hunt in which three hundred men died.

literal: Kudie Gan and Jing, while seated with Shenwu, asked to serve as censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: Kudie Gan and Jing, while seated with Gao Huan, asked to serve as censor-in-chief.

literal: Shenwu said, "Why do you seek so low an office?
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Why do you seek so low an office?

literal: " Gan said, "To arrest Wei Jing.
idiomatic: " Kudie Gan said, "To arrest Wei Jing.

literal: " Shenwu laughed greatly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock them.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan laughed greatly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock them.

literal: Dongtong stripped Jing's clothes and said, "You strip the common people — why should Dongtong not strip you!
idiomatic: Dongtong stripped Jing's clothes and said, "You strip the common people — why should Dongtong not strip you!

literal: " Shenwu admonished Jing, "You can do without greed.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan admonished Jing, "You can do without greed.

literal: " Jing said, "When we reckon whose way of living brings in more, I only take from people; you carve off the emperor's taxes.
idiomatic: " Jing said, "When we reckon whose way of living brings in more, I only take from people; you carve off the emperor's taxes.

literal: " Shenwu smiled and did not answer.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan smiled and did not answer.

literal: His title was changed to Duke of Changle Commandery.
idiomatic: His title was changed to duke of Changle Commandery.

literal: He rose in succession to grand guardian and grand tutor, then was imprisoned for concealing a fugitive.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to grand guardian and grand tutor, then was imprisoned for concealing a fugitive.

literal: He had Cui Xian tell Wenshuang, "Tell Ahuier — does his wealth and power mean to kill me!
idiomatic: He had Cui Xian tell Gao Cheng, "Tell Ahuier — does his wealth and power mean to kill me!

literal: " Shenwu heard and wept; he went to the palace and said, "Were it not for Wei Jing, your subject would never have reached today.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan heard and wept; he went to the palace and said, "Were it not for Wei Jing, your subject would never have reached today.

literal: " After three petitions the emperor granted it.
idiomatic: " After three petitions the emperor granted it.

literal: Thereupon he was demoted to general of the imperial horse and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.
idiomatic: Thereupon he was demoted to general of the imperial horse and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: Shenwu visited him; Jing lay in anger and would not rise, shouting, "If you're going to kill me, hurry up!
idiomatic: Gao Huan visited him; Jing lay in anger and would not rise, shouting, "If you're going to kill me, hurry up!

literal: " Lady Changshan said to Shenwu, "The old man is near death — how can you press him so cruelly?
idiomatic: " Lady Changshan said to Gao Huan, "The old man is near death — how can you press him so cruelly?

literal: " She also said, "I drew water for you until calluses formed on my hands.
idiomatic: " She also said, "I drew water for you until calluses formed on my hands.

literal: " She then showed her palms.
idiomatic: " She then showed her palms.

literal: Shenwu comforted Jing and knelt before him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan comforted Jing and knelt before him.

literal: Before this Jing had a pony; Wenshuang asked for it, and Jing would not give it, saying, "Earth piled together makes a wall; men supporting one another make a king — not even one horse may be kept and then demanded back.
idiomatic: Before this Jing had a pony; Gao Cheng asked for it, and Jing would not give it, saying, "Earth piled together makes a wall; men supporting one another make a king — not even one horse may be kept and then demanded back.

literal: " Shenwu, before Jing and Lady Changshan, rebuked Wenshuang and had him beaten.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan, before Jing and Lady Changshan, rebuked Gao Cheng and had him beaten.

literal: Lady Changshan wept and pleaded for him.
idiomatic: Lady Changshan wept and pleaded for him.

literal: Jing said, "The boy is used to indulgence — let him learn to be a trusted man; why all this weeping and wailing to stop a beating!
idiomatic: Jing said, "The boy is used to indulgence — let him learn to be a trusted man; why all this weeping and wailing to stop a beating!

literal: " Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qing Province; his conduct improved greatly, and the people lived at ease.
idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qing Province; his conduct improved greatly, and the people lived at ease.

literal: Summoned back, he was made grand marshal.
idiomatic: Summoned back, he was made grand marshal.

literal: He fell ill and died in the province.
idiomatic: He fell ill and died in the province.

literal: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor and director of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor and director of the masters of writing.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, because Jing was an original meritorious minister, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, because Jing was an original meritorious minister, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Shenwu's temple court and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court and posthumously enfeoffed prince of Changle.

literal: His son Can, from youth, held prominent posts; by nature he was coarse and martial.
idiomatic: His son Can, from youth, held prominent posts; by nature he was coarse and martial.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Kudie Gan and others were enfeoffed as princes; Can, because his father had not received a princely title, was greatly resentful and for more than ten days shut his door and did not attend court.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, Kudie Gan and others were enfeoffed as princes; Can, because his father had not received a princely title, was greatly resentful and for more than ten days shut his door and did not attend court.

literal: The emperor thought it strange and sent an envoy to his house to inquire.
idiomatic: The emperor thought it strange and sent an envoy to his house to inquire.

literal: Through the closed door he told the envoy, "If the Son of Heaven will not enfeoff Can's father as a prince, Can would rather die.
idiomatic: Through the closed door he told the envoy, "If the Son of Heaven will not enfeoff Can's father as a prince, Can would rather die.

literal: " The envoy said, "You must open the door to receive the edict.
idiomatic: " The envoy said, "You must open the door to receive the edict.

literal: " Can thereupon bent his bow and shot at the envoy through the door.
idiomatic: " Can thereupon bent his bow and shot at the envoy through the door.

literal: The envoy reported the matter; Wenxuan sent Duan Shao to deliver the imperial message.
idiomatic: The envoy reported the matter; Gao Yang sent Duan Shao to deliver the imperial message.

literal: When Can saw Shao, he only beat his breast and wept loudly, answering not a word.
idiomatic: When Can saw Shao, he only beat his breast and wept loudly, answering not a word.

literal: Wenxuan personally visited his house to comfort him; only then did he resume attending court.
idiomatic: Gao Yang personally visited his house to comfort him; only then did he resume attending court.

literal: Soon afterward Jing was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: Soon afterward Jing was posthumously enfeoffed prince of Changle.

literal: Can inherited the title.
idiomatic: Can inherited the title.

literal: He rose to minister of education and grand tutor, then died.
idiomatic: He rose to minister of education and grand tutor, then died.

literal: His son Shibian succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Shibian succeeded.

literal: When the Zhou army was about to enter Ye, Shibian was ordered out with more than a thousand horsemen to reconnoiter; leaving by Fukou, he climbed a high mound and looked west; seeing flocks of birds rise in the distance, he took them for the banners of the Western army and galloped back — by the time he reached Zimo Bridge he dared not look behind him.
idiomatic: When the Zhou army was about to enter Ye, Shibian was ordered out with more than a thousand horsemen to reconnoiter; leaving by Fukou, he climbed a high mound and looked west; seeing flocks of birds rise in the distance, he took them for the banners of the Western army and galloped back — by the time he reached Zimo Bridge he dared not look behind him.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as governor of Zhe Province.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as governor of Zhe Province.

literal: Lou Zhao, styled Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the maternal younger brother of Empress Lou Wuming.
idiomatic: Lou Zhao, styled Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the maternal younger brother of Empress Lou Wuming.

literal: His grandfather Ti was bold and far-sighted; his household had a thousand servants, and cattle and horses were counted by the bushel.
idiomatic: His grandfather Ti was bold and far-sighted; his household had a thousand servants, and cattle and horses were counted by the bushel.

literal: By nature he delighted in giving to others; many men of worth attached themselves to him.
idiomatic: By nature he delighted in giving to others; many men of worth attached themselves to him.

literal: In the reign of Emperor Taiwu of Wei he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhending for merit.
idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Taiwu of Wei he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhending for merit.

literal: His father Neigan possessed martial strength but died before holding office.
idiomatic: His father Neigan possessed martial strength but died before holding office.

literal: When Zhao rose high, the Wei court posthumously made Neigan minister of education.
idiomatic: When Lou Zhao rose high, the Wei court posthumously made his father Neigan minister of education.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, Neigan was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Lou Zhao's father Neigan was posthumously enfeoffed prince of Taiyuan.

literal: Zhao was dignified, upright, and of great bearing, with deep designs; his belt was eight feet long, and in archery and horsemanship he stood first in the age.
idiomatic: Lou Zhao was dignified, upright, and of great bearing, with deep designs; his belt was eight feet long, and in archery and horsemanship he stood first in the age.

literal: From youth Shenwu treated him with close regard.
idiomatic: From youth Gao Huan treated him with close regard.

literal: Zhao also recognized men early and always showed them full courtesy and respect.
idiomatic: Lou Zhao also recognized men early and always showed them full courtesy and respect.

literal: He often followed Shenwu on hunts and each time urged that one should not ride through danger or up steep slopes.
idiomatic: He often followed Gao Huan on hunts and each time urged that one should not ride through danger or up steep slopes.

literal: The second son Dingyuan, from youth, held prominent posts; among the imperial kin he was especially favored and intimate with Wucheng.
idiomatic: The second son Dingyuan, from youth, held prominent posts; among the imperial kin he was especially favored and intimate with Gao Zhan.

literal: He was separately enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai Commandery.
idiomatic: He was separately enfeoffed prince of Linhuai Commandery.
